messages:
ivan: Heads up, CI perf dashboard shows a small-seq tail-latency spike on the CUDA/driver upgrade job (driver 12.15.p4) after the rollout yesterday.

jess: Saw that too. 95th/99th up ~2.5-3x for tiny batches (1-4).

leah: Any obvious kernel changes in the flamegraphs?

ivan: Quick look points at more time in async IO code and a new kv-meta contention peak. attaching quick sample:

```
kv_meta_lock.acquire 12.3ms
kv_meta_lock.wait   8.9ms
prefetch_coalesce.batch_size 18
async_io.window_ms 12
```

sam: That async_io.window_ms bump smells like the coalescing tweak from PR #4567 (landed in runtime scheduler). could be increasing hold time on metadata locks.

perf-bot: perf-ci: regression detected on job runtime-smallseq-upgrade (compare: baseline -> driver12.15.p4), 99p latency +210% (p < 0.01).

jess: Can someone run a quick nsys trace on the failing job? Prefer end-to-end trace with our kvcache markers.

leah: Running now on canary node r-io-42. Command:

```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=cpu --output=kvmeta_spike /opt/redwood/bin/runtime_test --profile-kv
```

ivan: Also added a lightweight perf mark in the runtime to log kv_meta_lock hold times so we can correlate timelines.

sam: Trace uploaded: link to internal artifact (s3://perf-artifacts/3302109876/nsys.kvmeta.zip) :eyes: preliminary view shows repeated short convoys where one request holds kv meta for ~10-20ms and following requests queue up.

jess: Does this reproduce on older driver when we force the new scheduler? i.e., isolate driver vs scheduler change.

ivan: Good call. I spun up a node with previous driver (12.14) but same runtime build -> no spike. Then runtime older build with driver 12.15.p4 -> also no spike. Means interaction between driver and the new async coalescing path.

leah: So it's a cross-layer regression. theory: some kernel path in the driver causes slightly longer IO completion callbacks which stretch the coalescing window and increase lock hold time. That then serializes tiny seq work.

sam: Quick repro: reduce async_io.window_ms from 12 -> 4 on canary config. Results: 99p back down to baseline within 30 minutes.

jess: Nice. Can we convert that into a runtime mitigation toggle so we can unstick rollouts until we get a proper fix?

ivan: I pushed a hotfix branch that gates the coalescer behind a feature flag and lowers default window_ms for driver >= 12.15.p4. Branch: git://redwood/runtime fix/coalesce-gate-3302.

perf-bot: perf-ci: ran canary job with fix branch -> 99p latency within 5% of baseline.

deploy-bot: Rollout paused automatically for release v1.84 due to perf regression. Manual hold placed by @jess.

jess: I'm leaving the rollout on hold. tagging eng-sre for visibility.

leah: Plan: 1) ship hotfix gate for immediate unblocking 2) open issue with driver vendor with attached nsys traces 3) write a small microbenchmark to exercise completion callback timing 4) follow up with a proper scheduling change if vendor can't address soon.

sam: I'll open the revert PR with the gate and run canary + morning smoke.

ivan: Thanks. Also adding a test that asserts kv_meta_lock median < 1ms for tiny sequences so we catch future regressions in CI.

jess: :thumbsup: good runbook. if vendor replies we can enable full coalescing back behind an opt-in. for now keep the gate and low window in the runtime defaults.

leah: Adding labels: regression, rollout-blocker, driver-interaction, bisect-complete.

sam: PR out: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4891 - includes gate, config flag, test, and canary run results in the description.

ivan: Once merged I'll unhold the rollout and watch the dashboard for 2 hours before full resume.

jess: Cool. closing loop when rollout resumes. thanks everyone.
